about: Animated look (how-to card): the compounding curve and the melting ice cube.

scenes.narration: Tiny improvements compound. But the payoff shows up late.
James Clear starts with a simple idea. Get about one percent better every day, and it adds up to something big. Small daily slips add up too, the other way.

params.title: What you expect vs. what happens

scenes.narration: The catch is timing. Early on, the results are almost invisible. Many people quit right here, just before the effort starts to pay off.
Think of an ice cube in a cold room. You warm the room, degree by degree, and nothing happens. Then, at freezing point, it melts. The earlier warming was doing the work all along.

lines: The work just hasn't surfaced yet.

scenes.narration: So if you feel stuck, your effort may simply not have surfaced yet.
Pick one skill, and make one tiny improvement today. Write down the date, so you can look back in three months.
